subject: general
question: The Planning Commission was established to steer India's five year plans. Who was the first chairman of the Planning Commission of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jawaharlal Nehru**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru was the first chairman of the Planning Commission of India, as the position of chairman was traditionally held by the Prime Minister of India.
 
• The Planning Commission was established on **15 March 1950**, with the aim of formulating and overseeing India’s Five-Year Plans.
 
• The first Five-Year Plan (1951-1956), under Nehru’s leadership, focused on agricultural development and infrastructure building to address food shortages and boost economic growth.
 
• The Planning Commission was later replaced by the **NITI Aayog** (National Institution for Transforming India) in **2015** under Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
 
• As the first Prime Minister of independent India, Nehru played a pivotal role in shaping the country’s economic policies through the Planning Commission.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Planning Commission:**

 
 
• It was a non-constitutional and non-statutory body tasked with assessing resources and formulating development plans for India.
 
• The commission was headquartered in New Delhi and worked under the direct supervision of the Prime Minister.
 
• It operated through the formulation of Five-Year Plans to address sectors like agriculture, industry, education, and health.
 
 
 
• **Five-Year Plans:**
 
 
• The First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956) focused on agriculture, irrigation, and energy to rebuild India's economy post-independence.
 
• The Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961), also known as the Mahalanobis Plan, emphasized rapid industrialization.
 
• These plans aimed to achieve self-sufficiency, equitable distribution of resources, and sustainable growth.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog:**
 
 
• It replaced the Planning Commission on **1 January 2015** to promote cooperative federalism and align with India’s changing economic needs.
 
• NITI Aayog focuses on policy think-tanks, innovation, and partnerships with states for development.
 
 
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru’s Vision:**
 
 
• Nehru’s vision for India emphasized industrialization, scientific development, and modern economic strategies to uplift the nation.
 
• He viewed planning as a means to achieve social justice, reduce inequality, and accelerate progress.
